name: ckan/ckanapi
what_it_holds: Official CLI + Python module for the CKAN Action API (CKAN is the open-data portal platform used by many EU cities/national statistics offices and some US agencies). Supports bulk dataset dump/load, remote/local/test targets, parallel workers. 212 stars, 615 commits, MIT/Crown Copyright license, active CI.
why_useful: Complements sodapy for CKAN-based portals; several EU STR-regulation and housing-registry sources (city/regional open-data catalogues in scope per gap #12/#13) are CKAN-hosted, so this is a working discovery/pull method rather than a bespoke scraper.
geography: Global (client works against any CKAN-hosted portal)
themes: Housing affordability and STR-housing studies data: rent-burden, vacancy, STR share of housing stock by tract
Open-data portal discovery: Socrata/CKAN/data.gov/EU data portal clients, dataset search tools, Google Dataset Search scrapers; city portals with STR datasets
Short-term-rental insurance/incident, noise complaint and 311 datasets mentioning Airbnb (NYC 311, LA MyLA311, SF 311) as enforcement/activity proxies
why_all: Complements sodapy for CKAN-based portals; several EU STR-regulation and housing-registry sources (city/regional open-data catalogues in scope per gap #12/#13) are CKAN-hosted, so this is a working discovery/pull method rather than a bespoke scraper.

Standard tooling for bulk-pulling from CKAN-based portals (US data.gov, many EU/UK/Canada city and national statistics portals) that could hold STR registries, tourism-board releases, or housing datasets under gaps 7, 12, 13.

Complements sodapy for gap #17 — lets an agent discover and pull STR/complaint datasets from CKAN-based city portals outside the Socrata set (useful for the EU registration/enforcement trackers in gap #12), rounding out a cross-city 311/enforcement-proxy pull pipeline.

name: uscensusbureau/citysdk
what_it_holds: Official (now archived) Census Bureau JavaScript utility library for Census APIs: statistics pulls plus cartographic GeoJSON and lat/lng-to-FIPS geocoding.
why_useful: Geocoding utility to map STR listing lat/lng (Inside Airbnb) to census tract/FIPS for joining against ACS vacancy/rent-burden tables; superseded functionally by tidycensus but still a working reference implementation.
license: not confirmed in fetch (US Census Bureau official repo)
duplicate_of_holding: tidycensus does the statistical-pull half better and is actively maintained; citysdk's only distinct value is the lat/lng->FIPS geocoding helper
themes: Housing affordability and STR-housing studies data: rent-burden, vacancy, STR share of housing stock by tract
why_all: Geocoding utility to map STR listing lat/lng (Inside Airbnb) to census tract/FIPS for joining against ACS vacancy/rent-burden tables; superseded functionally by tidycensus but still a working reference implementation.

name: weekly-economic-index-gdp-nowcasting
what_it_holds: Apache-2.0 licensed repo (last updated 2 Aug 2026) implementing GDP nowcasting from a weekly economic index construction; description is empty, so exact data source (own WEI-style build vs. pulling NY Fed's WEI) and file contents were not confirmed via README/API inspection.
why_useful: Potential open replication of a WEI-style weekly GDP nowcast methodology (relevant to gap #17 mixed-frequency/nowcasting methods); worth a closer look by whoever picks up this thread, but not verified to contain a usable dataset.
themes: Real-time and weekly economic indicators: OECD Weekly Tracker (Google Trends based), NY Fed WEI, ONS faster indicators, Dallas Fed mobility, Bundesbank weekly activity index

name: covid-lockdown-asset-pricing
what_it_holds: Markov-chain asset-pricing analysis using the FRED-hosted NY Fed Weekly Economic Index (WEI) for the COVID period; likely just pulls WEI from FRED (a series we may already have access to via our existing FRED integration) rather than storing an independent longer history.
why_useful: Confirms the WEI is trivially available through FRED (which the project already queries for ~40 series) — worth adding the WEI series ID to our existing FRED pull rather than treating this as a new data source; the repo itself is a one-off academic analysis, not a data store.
duplicate_of_holding: FRED (already integrated) hosts NY Fed WEI directly; no separate data value in this repo
themes: Real-time and weekly economic indicators: OECD Weekly Tracker (Google Trends based), NY Fed WEI, ONS faster indicators, Dallas Fed mobility, Bundesbank weekly activity index

name: fbi (Factor-Based Imputation) R package
what_it_holds: R package (GPL-3.0, 70 commits) implementing Bai-Ng-style factor/matrix-completion imputation for high-dimensional macro panels; ships a vignette applying the method to the FRED-MD monthly macro dataset (McCracken & Ng), though the FRED-MD data itself is fetched externally, not committed.
why_useful: Could be applied to reconstruct/impute gaps in a weekly or monthly macro panel we assemble (e.g. filling missing weeks in a homemade weekly tracker), tangential fit to point-in-time vintage work (gap #4).
geography: n/a (generic method); demo uses US FRED-MD
themes: Real-time and weekly economic indicators: OECD Weekly Tracker (Google Trends based), NY Fed WEI, ONS faster indicators, Dallas Fed mobility, Bundesbank weekly activity index
Point-in-time macro vintages: ALFRED tooling, Philly Fed real-time dataset, ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages; packages for vintage-aware backtests
FRED / BEA / BLS / Census API clients and curated macro panels (consumer sentiment, PCE services, CPI lodging, airfares, unemployment by metro)
why_all: Could be applied to reconstruct/impute gaps in a weekly or monthly macro panel we assemble (e.g. filling missing weeks in a homemade weekly tracker), tangential fit to point-in-time vintage work (gap #4).

Useful methods layer if the team pulls the (separately hosted) FRED-MD/FRED-QD standardized macro panels and needs missing-value handling consistent with the academic real-time-data literature; adjacent to point-in-time macro nowcasting methods (gap #17).

Points to FRED-MD/FRED-QD (large curated 100+ series monthly/quarterly macro panels, standard in macro-nowcasting) as an external target, plus a working imputation method for handling ragged-edge/missing macro data in a MIDAS/DFM nowcast — relevant to gap #17 (mixed-frequency nowcasting methods).
